summary: An Indologist, Dieter George held a post at the Berlin State Library from around 1969 to 1985 and was attested in 1985 as the successor to Wolfgang Voigt.

Dieter Schlingloff is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. He was a scientific co-worker at the German Academy of Sciences at Berlin (~1955-1959) and held posts at the University of Kiel (~1967-1972) and Munich (~1972-1996).

Tibetologist Dieter Schuh studied under Shri Krishna Sharma at the University of Cologne (~1967-1972). He served as a special professor in Tibetology at the University of Bonn (~1978-2007) and founded the International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies.

Dietmar Rothermund was a historian and Indologist who studied at Marburg, Munich, and the University of Pennsylvania, where he earned his PhD in 1959. He was affiliated with Heidelberg University, attested in 2004.
Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Shechen Gyaltsap Gyurme Pema Namgyal, Khenpo Shenga, and Dzongsar Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö (~1926-1959).

Archaeologist and Indologist Dilip K. Chakrabarti studied at the University of Calcutta (~1959-1965). He held posts at Calcutta (~1965-1977), the University of Delhi (~1977-1990), and Cambridge (~1990-2007) as Professor of South Asian Archaeology.
Dilip Kumar Roy worked in archaeology and Indology, serving in the Department of Museology at the University of Calcutta, where he was attested as Reader in 1982 and attested again in 1994.
Dilli Raman Regmi was an Indologist and historian who completed an M.A. at Patna University and an M.Litt at the University of Madras.

Dina Bangdel was a scholar of religious studies and archaeology. She held a post at Virginia Commonwealth University from around 2002 to 2017, and an affiliation with Ohio State University is attested in 2006.

Dines Andersen was a Danish scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen (~1879-1892) under Vilhelm Thomsen, Karl Verner, and Michael Viggo Fausbøll, later serving there as professor of Indian philology (1903-1927).

Indologist and historian Dineschandra Sircar was Government Epigraphist for India at the Archaeological Survey of India (until 1961, attested 1963) and held posts at the University of Calcutta, including Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture from 1962.

Ding-hwa Evelyn Hsieh, a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies, completed a PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles. In 1998, she was appointed professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University.
A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Dipak Kumar Barua served as Dean at the University of Calcutta in 1987 and as head of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara around 1996.

Dipak Ranjan Das, a scholar in archaeology and Indology, studied under Dineschandra Sircar. He held a post in the Department of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta, attested in 1994.

Historian Dipesh Chakrabarty studied at Calcutta, IIM Calcutta, and the Australian National University (~1977-1980). He taught at the University of Melbourne (~1983-1995) and held a post at the University of Chicago starting in 1995.

Dirk H. A. Kolff is an Indologist and historian who earned an MA at Leiden University (~1960-1967). He served at Leiden as Professor of Modern Indian History in 1967 and held a post there from 1991 to 2003.

Diwakar Acharya, working in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, earned a PhD at Hamburg (~2000-2004) under Ramananda Giri. He held posts at Nepal Sanskrit University, Hamburg, Kyoto University (2006-2016), and Oxford (~2016), succeeding Alexis Sanderson.
Dixian was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Mingzu and served as abbot of Guanzong Temple from around 1913 to 1932.

Indologist Dominic Goodall completed his D.Phil. at Oxford (-1995) under Alexis Sanderson and also studied under Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan. He served as a lecturer at EPHE (2005) and held a professorship at the EFEO starting in 2000.

Dominic Sur works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Harvard and the University of Virginia under David Germano, Karen C. Lang, Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and Khenpo Lama Chönam, later holding a post at Utah State University (attested 2017).
